sources.access: Publisher author abstract and references, free to read

sources.title: Towards knowledge autonomy in the Companion cognitive architecture
sources.access: Indexed publisher metadata, highlights and selected excerpts; direct DOI redirect blocked; full methods unavailable

implemented: Authors report analogical learning across bounded tasks; 2025 describes knowledge management and a SocialBot with limited opportunities to seek and accept knowledge.
learned: Reported acquisition and organization of knowledge within a designed representation, with limited self-directed acquisition; exact quantitative results not established here.
designed: Qualitative descriptions, analogical processing, symbolic knowledge stack including CycL and NextKB, retrieval and management tools.
limit: The 2017 and 2025 authors explicitly describe their ultimate objectives as unfinished. Full knowledge autonomy, endogenous objectives, and acquisition of the learning machinery are not established.
ora: Distinguish learning independently from developing the mechanism that enables learning; distinguish autonomy of knowledge management from general autonomy.
rights: Lawful public author abstracts, institutional records and selected proceedings text; metadata and original analysis only, no full documents reproduced.

sources.authors: Pablo Bustos; Luis J. Manso; Antonio J. Bandera; Juan P. Bandera; Ismael García-Varea; Jesús Martínez-Gómez
sources.institution: Universities of Extremadura, Málaga, Castilla-La Mancha; Aston University
sources.title: The CORTEX Cognitive Robotics Architecture: use cases
sources.access: Institutional publication record and author abstract; accepted manuscript linked, not fully reviewed; record labels CC BY-NC-ND

implemented: Authors describe tested physical human-robot interaction scenarios using interconnected modules and a shared graph encoding geometric and symbolic state.
learned: No autonomous invention of new capabilities established by the abstract; updating a dynamic state graph is not in itself retained learning.
designed: Functional decomposition selected in advance, module communication constraints, graph representation, sensors and effectors.
limit: Reported use cases do not demonstrate acquisition of new cognitive mechanisms or open-ended development. Full methods and controls not audited.
ora: Distinguish dynamic internal state representation from long-term acquisition of new representations or operators.
rights: Lawful public author abstracts, institutional records and selected proceedings text; metadata and original analysis only, no full documents reproduced.

sources.title: Cognitive systems for cognitive assistants
sources.funding: EU contribution EUR 6,224,000 across consortium; total EUR 7,490,000; coordinator Kungliga Tekniska Hoegskolan, Sweden; Birmingham and other author institutions listed as participants

implemented: Physical tabletop robot combines concurrent specialized components. Authors show teaching object colour, then using learned visual properties in a manipulation instruction.
learned: Cross-modal mappings for selected object attributes acquired in dialogue with a human tutor, then used in a subsequent action; most other ontology mappings were authored.
designed: Component architecture, shared feature vocabulary, mapping conventions, task-manager rules, learning algorithms and tutor-supplied labels; initial reference assumption selects most recently presented object.
limit: The architecture schema does not itself contain learning mechanisms; implementations supply them. Bounded example, not evidence of unassisted concept invention or independent objectives. Figure dialogue and prose have inconsistent red/blue example wording; do not infer exact sequence beyond the learning-to-use distinction. No final contractual acceptance recovered.
ora: Strong comparator for actually learned cross-modal associations versus authored translation scaffolding; distinguish extension by developers adding modules from development by an individual agent.
rights: Lawful public author abstracts, institutional records and selected proceedings text; metadata and original analysis only, no full documents reproduced.

sources.authors: Matthias Scheutz; Thomas Williams; Evan Krause; Brley Oosterveld (lab metadata spelling); Vasanth Sarathy; Tyler Frasca
sources.title: An Overview of the Distributed Integrated Affect and Reflection Cognitive DIARC Architecture
sources.identifier: Springer Cognitive Architectures chapter, lab key scheutzetal2018diarcchapter
sources.access: Author laboratory bibliographic record and abstract; separate Colorado School of Mines lab record gives Bradley Oosterveld

implemented: 2018 authors demonstrate learning objects and actions through spoken instructions on a physical robot; example shows unknown higher-level task and nested teaching of an unknown subtask.
learned: New procedure composition and object knowledge via explicit human instruction, rather than repeated independent trial-and-error.
designed: Language interpretation, perceptual and action primitives, instruction-based learning and composition machinery; teacher specifies sequence and task.
limit: No evidence here of independently discovering the instructed task objective or inventing primitive motor machinery; no independent replication or verified long-term retention. Exact award not established.
ora: Novel combinations of known primitives can be meaningful acquired competence even if a teacher specifies the procedure; keep teacher provenance distinct from spontaneous exploration.
rights: Lawful public author abstracts, institutional records and selected proceedings text; metadata and original analysis only, no full documents reproduced.

sources.title: DiPRA: A Layered Agent Architecture which Integrates Practical Reasoning and Sensorimotor Schemas
sources.access: CNR record and indexed publisher text; direct publisher route blocked; no full method audit

implemented: Concurrent goal, plan, action and belief modules under graded activity and a central deliberation component; simulation illustrates practical reasoning under conflicting goals.
learned: Environmental feedback updates beliefs and relevance and activates instrumental goals; no demonstrated durable acquisition of new objectives or operators.
designed: Goal conditions, action and plan structure, fuzzy cognitive map, activation and resource allocation rules, world interface.
limit: Case study is a bounded simulation; reported emergent coordination is not independent origin of objectives. Programme funding and publication linkage do not establish final contractual outcomes.
ora: Relevant competing explanation for seemingly endogenous goal changes: contextual weighting among authored objectives and subgoals.
